sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是 99% Invisible。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This is part three of the 2020-2021 mini-stories episodes,
sentences.zh: 这是 2020-2021 迷你故事系列的第三部分，

sentences.en: where I interview the staff about their favorite little stories from the built world that don't quite fill out an entire episode for whatever reason,
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我采访了工作人员，让他们聊聊那些他们最喜欢的、关于建筑世界的微小故事；不知出于什么原因，这些故事虽然撑不起整整一集，

sentences.en: but are great 99PI stories nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 但它们依然是非常精彩的 99PI 故事。

sentences.en: We have music games with Sean Reale, Lost Statues with Joe Rosenberg, and Overactive Heaters with Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 我们有肖恩·雷尔带来的音乐游戏，乔·罗森伯格带来的失落雕像，以及德兰妮·霍尔带来的过热暖气片。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Hey Dee, what do you have for us today?
sentences.zh: 嘿，迪，今天给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: So today I want to talk with you about old radiators, and have you ever lived with an old radiator?
sentences.zh: 今天我想和你聊聊旧暖气片，你以前住的地方有用过旧暖气片吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 用过。

sentences.en: Where we met, like, I don't know, 15 years ago in Chicago, when we worked together at the station there, I lived in at least one apartment that had a radiator, which was, yeah,
sentences.zh: 我们俩相识的时候——大概，我记不清了，15 年前在芝加哥，当时我们在那里的电台一起工作——我住过至少一间有暖气片的公寓，当时，对，

sentences.en: it was a confounding device.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个让人摸不透的装置。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they are notorious for being loud, you know, like clanking a lot, and also just for being too hot.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，它们出了名的吵，你知道的，比如会发出很多哐啷哐啷的杂音，而且还总是太热。

sentences.en: Yeah, blisteringly hot.
sentences.zh: 对，热得让人发烫。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So I don't know if you've ever wondered why that is, but I recently learned that there is a reason for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道你有没有想过为什么会这样，但我最近了解到这背后是有原因的。

sentences.en: And it's actually related not to this current pandemic we're all living through, but to the flu pandemic of 1918 and 1919.
sentences.zh: 而且它其实跟我们现在正经历的这场大流行病无关，而是与 1918 年和 1919 年的流感大流行有关。

sentences.en: Well, I've heard a little bit about this, but I don't know the full story, so I'm excited that you're bringing this to us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我听说过一点这方面的消息，但不知道完整的故事，所以很高兴你能把这个带给我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So I, first of all, I learned about this history in an article in Bloomberg City Lab.
sentences.zh: 首先，我是从《彭博城市实验室》的一篇文章中了解到这段历史的。

sentences.en: It was reported by Patrick Sisson.
sentences.zh: 这是由帕特里克·西森报道的。

sentences.en: And it was kind of through that article that I found Dan Hollihan.
sentences.zh: 也就是通过那篇文章，我找到了丹·霍利汉。

sentences.en: So he grew up in the heating industry.
sentences.zh: 他是在暖气行业长大的。

sentences.en: His dad worked for this plumbing and heating wholesaler in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲在曼哈顿的一家管道和暖气批发商工作。

sentences.en: And now his family runs a website called HeatingHelp.com.
sentences.zh: 现在他的家人经营着一个名为 HeatingHelp.com 的网站。

sentences.en: He wrote a book called The Lost Art of Steam Heat.
sentences.zh: 他写过一本书叫《蒸汽供暖的失落艺术》。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, he's just really into heating, specifically steam heating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，他就是对供暖非常入迷，尤其是蒸汽供暖。

sentences.en: It throws such a lovely, radiant glow on you.
sentences.zh: 它能散发出一种如此可爱、温暖的光芒照在你身上。

sentences.en: It's like being on the beach.
sentences.zh: 就像在海滩上一样。

sentences.en: And it's just a wonderful way to heat.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种绝佳的取暖方式。

sentences.en: And the dogs are always sleeping in front of it.
sentences.zh: 狗狗总是睡在它前面。

sentences.en: And the cat will pop up on top of it.
sentences.zh: 猫咪会跳到它上面去。

sentences.en: And people will dry their hats and gloves on top of it.
sentences.zh: 人们会在它上面烘干帽子和手套。

sentences.en: It's just a, it feels like home.
sentences.zh: 这真的有一种，家的感觉。

sentences.en: So he can go on and on waxing poetically about steam heat for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以滔滔不绝、充满诗意地大谈特谈蒸汽供暖很久。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: And he got really interested in the history of steam heating in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他对美国蒸汽供暖的历史产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: And he said that as he started doing this research, he was looking at these primary source documents, like these old technical manuals.
sentences.zh: 他说，当他开始做这项研究时，他查看了这些一手历史文献，比如那些旧的技术手册。

sentences.en: And he kept coming across references to the fresh air movement.
sentences.zh: 他不断地看到关于“新鲜空气运动”的引述。

sentences.en: I'm on board with the fresh air movement.
sentences.zh: 我完全支持“新鲜空气运动”。

sentences.en: I'd follow Terry Gross into the gates of hell.
sentences.zh: 让我追随特里·格罗斯进地狱大门我都愿意。

sentences.en: I think we're all part of the fresh air movement.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都是“新鲜空气运动”的一部分。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But this is a different fresh air movement.
sentences.zh: 但这是另一个“新鲜空气运动”。

sentences.en: Well, that's too bad.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那太遗憾了。

sentences.en: We'll have to work on the other one.
sentences.zh: 我们得去研究另一个了。

sentences.en: This one, not with Terry Gross, was a health crusade.
sentences.zh: 这个，可不是跟着特里·格罗斯，而是一场健康运动。

sentences.en: It started right after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 它始于内战刚结束时。

sentences.en: And proponents of the fresh air movement basically thought that stale, uncirculated air was bad, like very bad for your health.
sentences.zh: “新鲜空气运动”的倡导者基本上认为，陈旧、不流通的空气是不好的，对健康非常有害。

sentences.en: They called it vitiated air, which means spoiled air.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“被污染的空气”，意思就是变质的空气。

sentences.en: And they thought that spoiled air was everywhere, like we were just steeping in it.
sentences.zh: 他们认为变质的空气无处不在，就像我们泡在里面一样。

sentences.en: People didn't bathe regularly.
sentences.zh: 人们不经常洗澡。

sentences.en: There was unventilated stoves that would be in the place.
sentences.zh: 房间里会有没有通风管道的炉子。

sentences.en: So they just said it's dirty air, and it's coming off your body, and it's coming out of your mouth, and you're smoking,
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是说这是脏空气，它从你的身体里散发出来，从你的嘴里吐出来，你在抽烟，

sentences.en: and all these things are going on in a sealed apartment that doesn't have good circulation to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都发生在一个本来就没有良好通风的密闭公寓里。

sentences.en: So that caught everybody's attention because it was indeed killing people.
sentences.zh: 所以这引起了所有人的注意，因为它确实在夺去人们的生命。

sentences.en: And so this was pre-germ theory, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在当时还没有“细菌理论”，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was.
sentences.zh: 对，确实没有。

sentences.en: Did they have a concept of the mechanism of why unventilated air might be making them sick?
sentences.zh: 他们当时对“为什么没有通风的空气会让人生病”这种机制有什么概念吗？

sentences.en: They didn't really at this point.
sentences.zh: 他们当时其实并没有。

sentences.en: They were just sort of starting to realize that something was up.
sentences.zh: 他们只是开始意识到有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And one of the main proponents of the fresh air movement was a guy named Louis Leeds.
sentences.zh: “新鲜空气运动”的主要倡导者之一是一个叫路易斯·利兹的人。

sentences.en: He had been an inspector for the Union Army Field Hospitals, and he got really interested in this idea of vitiated air.
sentences.zh: 他曾是联邦军队野战医院的检查员，并对这种“被污染的空气”的概念产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: He was convinced that something about it was making people ill.
sentences.zh: 他坚信某种与之相关的东西正在让人类生病。

sentences.en: And he actually teamed up with Harriet Beecher Stowe, who wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他还与写过《汤姆叔叔的小屋》的哈里特·比彻·斯托进行了合作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they created this traveling roadshow.
sentences.zh: 他们创办了这个巡回演出的路演。

sentences.en: They would basically go across the country and give lectures with these magic lantern-type slides.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上会走遍全国，用这种魔术幻灯片类型的幻灯片进行演讲。

sentences.en: She got, like, mom and dad sitting in the parlor, and in crawls the baby in the long gown and the baby's bonnet.
sentences.zh: 她展示了比如爸爸妈妈坐在客厅里，然后一个穿着长袍和婴儿帽的婴儿爬了进来。

sentences.en: And the baby crawls into these vapors that are coming out of the man, and they're done in red.
sentences.zh: 婴儿爬进了那些从男人身上散发出来的蒸汽中，这些蒸汽是用红色画出来的。

sentences.en: So you see, it comes out of his mouth, and it goes to the floor.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，它从他的嘴里出来，落到了地板上。

sentences.en: And the baby crawls into this cloud, and the next slide, the baby just kind of topples over and dies.
sentences.zh: 婴儿爬进了这团云雾中，下一张幻灯片里，婴儿就直接倒下死掉了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's some extreme form of scared straight.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种极端的“恐吓教育”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, it was pretty effective.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这相当有效。

sentences.en: They really caught the attention of lots of people.
sentences.zh: 他们确实吸引了大量人群的注意。

sentences.en: And I was really struck by when Dan was describing these lantern slides that they would show.
sentences.zh: 当丹描述他们展示的这些幻灯片时，我真的很受触动。

sentences.en: It really actually reminded me of the coronavirus diagrams you'll see, where there's, like, two people talking to each other,
sentences.zh: 这实际上真的让我想起了你会看到的冠状病毒图表，上面有两个人互相交谈，

sentences.en: and they're sort of spewing red and blue virus droplets all over each other's face.
sentences.zh: 他们互相在对方脸上喷射红色和蓝色的病毒飞沫。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, that scarred me.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，那可吓到我了。

sentences.en: That in the 90s reports from, like, 2020, they would show the black lights on hotel rooms of all the organic splatter all over hotel rooMs.
sentences.zh: 还有 90 年代关于 2020 年左右的报道，它们会展示酒店房间里的黑光灯，照出酒店房间里到处都是有机飞溅物。

sentences.en: I'm scarred for life for that.
sentences.zh: 这给我留下了终下阴影。

sentences.en: So these were sort of, like, the 19th century version of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这些可以说是那东西的 19 世纪版本。

sentences.en: And they were part of what helped the fresh air movement really take hold.
sentences.zh: 它们是帮助“新鲜空气运动”真正站稳脚跟的一部分。

sentences.en: So it gets very popular.
sentences.zh: 所以它变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And it gets so popular that building designers actually started adapting their buildings to bring in more fresh air.
sentences.zh: 它变得如此受欢迎，以至于建筑设计者实际上开始改造他们的建筑以引入更多的新鲜空气。

sentences.en: The tenements suddenly, you know, as they come into their own, have to have air shafts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当贫民窟开始发展起来时，它们突然必须有天井通风井。

sentences.en: And you have to have more windows.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须有更多的窗户。

sentences.en: And you can't have these hobbles.
sentences.zh: 你不能再有这些违章搭建的小屋。

sentences.en: And, you know, like you see in the gangs of New York, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，就像你在《纽约黑帮》里看到的那样，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So things got better.
sentences.zh: 所以情况变好了。

sentences.en: But then, you know, it took a crisis like the Spanish flu to really kick it into high gear.
sentences.zh: 但随后，你知道的，需要像西班牙大流感这样的危机才能真正让它进入白热化阶段。

sentences.en: What's going on is around this time in the 19-teens, there are these two things that are happening concurrently.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，在 1910 年代左右，有两件事同时发生。

sentences.en: And one is the flu pandemic, which, of course, was a devastating global pandemic that was killing hundreds of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 一个是流感大流行，这当然是一场毁灭性的全球大流行，夺去了数十万人的生命。

sentences.en: And then at the same time, steam heating is really getting going.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，蒸汽供暖也真正蓬勃发展起来。

sentences.en: So steam heating systems are being installed in buildings across the country.
sentences.zh: 因此，蒸汽供暖系统正在全国各地的建筑中安装。

sentences.en: And health officials at the time were starting to push this idea that people needed to keep their windows open, even in the winter.
sentences.zh: 当时的卫生官员开始推行这样一种观点：人们需要保持窗户打开，即使在冬天也是如此。

sentences.en: And they needed to do that to increase ventilation and minimize flu spread.
sentences.zh: 他们需要这样做来增加通风并最大程度地减少流感传播。

sentences.en: And if people were going to be keeping their windows open through the winter, they needed, like, some pretty oversized radiators.
sentences.zh: 如果人们要在整个冬天都开着窗户，他们就需要一些相当超大尺寸的暖气片。

sentences.en: And they were saying that because of the fresh air movement,
sentences.zh: 他们这样说是因为根据“新鲜空气运动”，

sentences.en: we have to start designing systems big enough that they can heat the building on the coldest day of the year with the wind blowing and the windows open.
sentences.zh: 我们必须开始设计足够大的系统，以便它们能够在一年中最冷的一天、在刮风且窗户大开的情况下为建筑物供暖。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is why radiators, like even today, can be so overpowering because they need to be that hot for the windows to be open.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么暖气片，甚至在今天，也会让人觉得火力过猛，因为为了开窗它们必须那么热。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And many of those radiator systems were so sturdy and so well built that they are still in use today.
sentences.zh: 其中许多暖气片系统非常坚固且建造精良，以至于今天仍在使用。

sentences.en: But yeah, the one that was in my apartment was certainly put in in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，我公寓里的那个肯定是在 20世纪20 年代安装的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the kind of interesting thing is that once the pandemic was over.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，一旦大流行结束，

sentences.en: People began to wonder, why do we have the windows open?
sentences.zh: 人们开始纳闷，我们为什么要开着窗户？

sentences.en: Oh, that was because of the flu.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是为了流感。

sentences.en: But that's gone more than 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但那已经过去 10 年多了。

sentences.en: Close the window.
sentences.zh: 把窗户关上吧。

sentences.en: So they closed the window and now they're stifling because it's so hot.
sentences.zh: 于是他们关上了窗户，现在他们热得透不过气来，因为里面太热了。

sentences.en: Ask anybody that lives in a Manhattan apartment nowadays.
sentences.zh: 问问现在住在曼哈顿公寓里的任何人就知道了。

sentences.en: And so all of those, you know, stifling people started insisting that something be done about this.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有那些热得透不过气来的人开始坚持要求对这种情况采取措施。

sentences.en: And what ended up happening is that basically a whole industry arose to retrofit those big overpowering radiators.
sentences.zh: 最终发生的情况是，基本上整个行业都兴起是为了改造那些火力过猛的大型暖气片。

sentences.en: So companies began to develop the radiator covers and other people would paint their radiators with this special paint.
sentences.zh: 因此，各公司开始开发暖气片罩，其他人则用这种特殊的油漆来粉刷他们的暖气片。

sentences.en: But if you use something called a bronzing paint, specifically an aluminum bronzing paint, which has flakes of metal in it,
sentences.zh: 但如果你使用一种叫做古铜漆的东西，特别是含有金属薄片的铝质古铜漆，

sentences.en: that will reduce the radiator's ability to radiate by 20%.
sentences.zh: 那将会使暖气片的辐射散热能力降低 20%。

sentences.en: So just by painting the radiator silver with this special paint, you're downsizing it.
sentences.zh: 所以只需用这种特殊的银色油漆粉刷暖气片，你就在事实上缩小了它的功率。

sentences.en: And this is why radiators are all silver for the most part.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么暖气片大部分都是银色的原因。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I had no idea that was why they were silver.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道这就是它们是银色的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, they're very often silver.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们非常常见是银色的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 对，它们确实是。

sentences.en: But it also must be made worse by the fact that the building around it is becoming more thermally efficient.
sentences.zh: 但这也一定因为周围建筑的热工效率越来越高而变得更糟糕。

sentences.en: Like buildings, you know, trap more heat in than they used to.
sentences.zh: 就像建筑物，你知道的，比过去锁住了更多的热量。

sentences.en: And that must make it even worse.
sentences.zh: 那一定让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Compared to, you know, the 19-teens, buildings now are basically like hermetically sealed.
sentences.zh: 与 1910 年代相比，现在的建筑物基本上就像是密封的。

sentences.en: In some office buildings, you cannot open the windows.
sentences.zh: 在某些办公楼里，你根本打不开窗户。

sentences.en: It's not designed that way.
sentences.zh: 它设计就不是那样的。

sentences.en: It's not an option.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个选项。

sentences.en: And so, you know, as you can imagine, that has become an issue with our current pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你可以想象的那样，这已经成为我们当前大流行病中的一个问题。

sentences.en: You need a lot of air coming in.
sentences.zh: 你需要大量的空气进来。

sentences.en: You need fresh air.
sentences.zh: 你需要新鲜空气。

sentences.en: So, and many of these high-end modern buildings can't do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，许多这些高端现代建筑做不到这一点。

sentences.en: And then windows don't open.
sentences.zh: 而且窗户打不开。

sentences.en: So that's, you know, this is where we're faced right now is, okay, what do we do with that?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们现在面临的处境，好吧，我们该怎么处理它？

sentences.en: I have been wondering, like,
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，

sentences.en: if this current pandemic would shift us back a little bit more towards open-air buildings because the need for fresh air and space seems as necessary as it was in the 19-teens.

sentences.en: And then also, like, this continuing pressure to make them more energy efficient because of climate change.
sentences.zh: 还有就是，由于气候变化，继续施加压力使它们更具能源效率。

sentences.en: So it'll be interesting to watch what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以看着事情会如何发展将会非常有趣。

sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的事情之一是，在大流行和封锁刚开始的时候，我们制作了一系列节目，当时我们试图用许多方法来减缓大流行的蔓延，

sentences.zh: 这些方法太古老了。

sentences.zh: 感觉疫苗就像是现代科学的一项丰功伟绩。

sentences.zh: 是的，尤其是这些疫苗。

sentences.en: Yeah, these vaccines.
sentences.zh: 对，这些疫苗。

sentences.en: Just, like, stay away from each other, cover your faces, open the windows.

sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Because if you cast your memory back, uh, not actually to all that long ago, you will recall, uh, 99 PI produced a story about monuments to Lenin.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把记忆拉回到——其实并没有那么久远的过去，你会记得，99 PI 制作过一期关于列宁纪念碑的节目。

sentences.zh: 没，没错。

sentences.en: Julia Barton did that story for us.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅·巴顿为我们做了那个报道。

sentences.en: It's kind of about what happened to all those Lenin monuments in Eastern Europe after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 91.
sentences.zh: 它有点像是关于1991年苏联解体后，东欧那些列宁纪念碑都经历了什么。

sentences.en: As our listeners probably know, and probably know, even if they didn't hear that episode, after the Soviet Union collapsed, a great many of those statues of Lenin, busts of Lenin,
sentences.zh: 正如我们的听众可能知道的，即便他们没有听过那一期节目也大多能猜到，在苏联解体后，大量的列宁雕像、列宁半身像，

sentences.en: and really all sorts of monuments to Lenin were toppled.
sentences.zh: 以及各种各样的列宁纪念碑都被推倒了。

sentences.en: They were torn down or pulverized or even like-
sentences.zh: 它们被拆毁、粉碎，甚至像——

sentences.en: Dramatically.
sentences.zh: 非常戏剧化地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like tossed into the Black Sea and consigned to various other sad fates.
sentences.zh: 比如被扔进黑海，落得各种其他悲惨的下场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think what the story was centered on and what was interesting to me is that there are some still standing in Russia that the ones that weren't destroyed that,
sentences.zh: 而且我想这个故事的核心以及让我感兴趣的是，俄罗斯仍然有一些幸存的纪念碑，那些没有被摧毁的、

sentences.en: that were put in these Soviet nostalgia parks alongside statues of other former communist leaders.
sentences.zh: 被放置在这些苏联怀旧公园里，与其它前共产主义领导人的雕像摆在一起的纪念碑。

sentences.en: It was a way of dealing with this history, um, without completely destroying it.
sentences.zh: 这是处理这段历史的一种方式，嗯，而没有完全摧毁它。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: They kind of almost like bracketed it off.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎就像是把它给框起来了。

sentences.en: They put this kind of meta frame around it.
sentences.zh: 他们给它加了一种元框架。

sentences.en: And so, like, it was, everyone was able to, like, look at it and you could just project what, what you wanted onto it in this kind of safer space or something.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都可以看着它，你可以在这个相对安全的空间里把你想投射的东西投射到它上面，或者别的什么。

sentences.en: That is the main thing that most people know about these old Lenin monuments, which is that most of them are gone or defunct in one way or another.
sentences.zh: 这是大多数人对这些旧列宁纪念碑的唯一了解，那就是它们大多已经消失了，或者以这样或那样的方式不复存在了。

sentences.en: But I am here to tell you that there is one monument to Lenin that not only lives on, but I think it's safe to say it will not be toppled anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 但我今天要告诉你们的是，有一座列宁纪念碑不仅长存至今，而且我可以肯定地说，它在短期内绝不会被推倒。

sentences.en: It is arguably, arguably the most secure Lenin in the world.
sentences.zh: 它可以说是世界上最安全的列宁像了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So why is that?
sentences.zh: 那为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is this one survived and will probably survive amongst all the others that have been toppled?
sentences.zh: 为什么这座雕像能在其他所有被推倒的雕像中幸存下来，并且可能还会继续幸存下去？

sentences.en: Well, to answer that, first of all, let me ask you, have you ever heard of something called a pole of inaccessibility?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了回答这个问题，首先，我想问你，你听说过所谓的不访问极吗？

sentences.en: No, I haven't.
sentences.zh: 没有，我没听说过。

sentences.en: It sounds a little ominous.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点不祥。

sentences.en: What is the pole of inaccessibility?
sentences.zh: 什么是不访问极？

sentences.en: So a pole of inaccessibility, it's both ominous and not.
sentences.zh: 所以，不访问极，它既听起来不祥又并非如此。

sentences.en: It is the geographical term that indicates the location on a given landmass that is further from the coastline than any other spot on that landmass.
sentences.zh: 它是地理学术语，指的是某块陆地上距离海岸线比该陆地上任何其他地点都要远的位置。

sentences.en: So every continent and every island has its own pole of inaccessibility, or POI.
sentences.zh: 因此，每一个大陆和每一个岛屿都有其自己的不访问极，简称 POI。

sentences.en: So for example, North America's POI is on the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota.
sentences.zh: 例如，北美的极点位于南达科他州的松岭印第安人保留地。

sentences.en: It's 1,030 miles from the nearest coastline.
sentences.zh: 它距离最近的海岸线有 1,030 英里。

sentences.en: Asia has a POI in the desert of western China.
sentences.zh: 亚洲的不访问极位于中国西部的沙漠中。

sentences.en: It's about 1,500 miles from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 它距离海岸线大约 1,500 英里。

sentences.en: But, you know, even something like the island of Great Britain has its own pole of inaccessibility.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，甚至像大不列颠岛这样的小地方也有它自己的不访问极。

sentences.en: According to the British Ordnance Survey, it is near Church Flats Farm in the county of Derbyshire and is a mere 70 miles from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 根据英国地形测量局的数据，它位于德比郡的教堂平地农场附近，距离海岸线仅仅 70 英里。

sentences.en: It's not that inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 那并没有那么难以接近。

sentences.en: No, I think you could knock that one out pretty easily if you ever wanted to.
sentences.zh: 不，我想如果你想的话，随时都可以轻而易举地走到那里。

sentences.en: But anyway, the reason I bring this all up is because way back in 1958,
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我提起这一切的原因是，早在 1958 年，

sentences.en: a team of scientists from the Soviet Union became the first people to ever reach the southern pole of inaccessibility.
sentences.zh: 来自苏联的一支科学家队伍成为第一批到达南半球不访问极的人。

sentences.en: And so this is the POI for Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 这就是南极洲的不访问极。

sentences.en: Is it actually the south pole or not?
sentences.zh: 它实际上是南极点吗？

sentences.en: No, so the south pole is closer to the coast because if you think about it, like there's that like big chunk taken out of like one side of Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 不是，南极点离海岸更近，因为如果你仔细想想，南极洲的一侧有一个很大的缺口被挖空了。

sentences.en: It's a little lopsided, right?
sentences.zh: 它有点不对称，对吧？

sentences.en: It's got that chunk taken out of it.
sentences.zh: 它缺了一大块。

sentences.en: And so the south pole is actually much closer to that coastline than the pole of inaccessibility, which true to its name for these Russian scientists was really hard to get to.
sentences.zh: 所以南极点实际上比不访问极离海岸线近得多，而不访问极正如其名，对这些俄罗斯科学家来说真的很难到达。

sentences.en: It's like really inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 真的是极难到达。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, like it was.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: So by definition, further inland than the geographic south pole, plus, you know, it's Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 所以根据定义，它比地理上的南极点更深入内陆，而且，你知道，那是南极洲。

sentences.en: So, you know, it was already also on the higher and colder part of the continent.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它已经在该大陆更高、更冷的部分了。

sentences.en: And then the further you are from the shoreline, the colder it tends to get.
sentences.zh: 而且你离海岸线越远，通常就越冷。

sentences.en: So, you know, we made it to the south pole in 1911.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们在 1911 年到达了南极点。

sentences.en: But when the Soviets finally got to the southern pole of inaccessibility, that took them another half century to reach.
sentences.zh: 但当苏联人终于到达南半球的不访问极时，他们花了又一个半世纪才抵达。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it doesn't have a lot of symbolic virtue and it seems like a horrible place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜它没有什么象征价值，而且看起来是个可怕的地方。

sentences.en: So why would you bother?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么还要费劲去呢？

sentences.en: They weren't really in a rush to get there.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不急着去那里。

sentences.en: And apparently they weren't in a rush to stay there either.
sentences.zh: 显然他们也并不急着留在那儿。

sentences.en: Because once this team of Soviet scientists got there, they tried to set up this meteorological research station.
sentences.zh: 因为这支苏联科学家队伍一到那里，就试图建立这个气象研究站。

sentences.en: But it was like insanely cold.
sentences.zh: 但那里冷得发疯。

sentences.en: The average temperature was something like negative 72 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 平均气温大概是华氏零下 72 度。

sentences.en: Average.
sentences.zh: 平均气温。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's horrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: So, right.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: So like just after like 12 days, they were like, screw this.
sentences.zh: 仅仅过了 12 天，他们就觉得，去它的吧。

sentences.en: And they left.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就离开了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's smart.
sentences.zh: 对，这很明智。

sentences.en: Good call.
sentences.zh: 干得漂亮。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Excellent call.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But before they returned to civilization, they left behind a bust of Lenin.
sentences.zh: 但在他们返回文明世界之前，他们留下了一尊列宁半身像。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 理所当然。

sentences.en: It's just the Soviet thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这很苏维埃。

sentences.en: And so here, let me show you a photo of what it looked like.
sentences.zh: 来吧，我给你们看一张它当年的照片。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There it is.
sentences.zh: 它就在那儿。

sentences.en: There's Lenin.
sentences.zh: 那就是列宁。

sentences.en: A bust of Lenin right on the top of a kind of like a pedestal of some kind.
sentences.zh: 一尊列宁半身像就立在某种基座的顶端。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So that is actually the chimney of the research station and which they dragged all the way there thinking probably that they'd use it for longer than 12 days.
sentences.zh: 那其实是研究站的烟囱，他们把它一路拖到那里，可能以为他们会在那里使用超过 12 天。

sentences.en: But now it serves this function of making sure Lenin is as lofty and dignified as possible as he gazes out over the white expanse.
sentences.zh: 但现在它的作用是确保列宁在凝视广袤的白色大地时，尽可能显得高大和庄严。

sentences.en: I mean, despite the stark surroundings, I mean, this looked like just a classic Lenin bust, like generic Lenin buSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尽管周围环境荒凉，但这看起来就像是一个经典的列宁半身像，一个普通的列宁半身像。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，完全是。

sentences.en: The furrowed brow, the jutting chin.
sentences.zh: 紧锁的眉头，微翘的下巴。

sentences.en: It's almost like at the last second before they left, they just grabbed a spare Lenin off the shelf and just kind of took it with them.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像他们在离开前的最后一秒，随便从架子上抓了一个备用的列宁像带走了。

sentences.en: So, you know, so I confess, yeah, it's not much to look at, but I kind of think of it as like the gargoyle on the top of a cathedral because like after they left,
sentences.zh: 所以，我承认，是的，这没什么好看的，但我有点把它看作大教堂顶上的怪兽滴水嘴，因为在他们离开后，

sentences.en: it was never intended to be seen by anyone.
sentences.zh: 它从来没打算被任何人看到。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like the gargoyle has a function, but the people on the ground can't see gargoyles.
sentences.zh: 就像滴水兽有其功能，但地面上的人看不到滴水兽一样。

sentences.en: They're meant for the designer of the church and maybe for God.
sentences.zh: 它们是为教堂的设计师准备的，也许是为上帝准备的。

sentences.en: And and that's it.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Or in the case of this Lenin, like, you know, pleasing to the materialist forces of Marxist Leninism.
sentences.zh: 或者就这个列宁像而言，满足了马克思列宁主义的唯物主义力量。

sentences.en: They, you know, you know, it sounds like I'm joking, but like they even oriented it so that it would forever face towards Moscow.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是在开玩笑，但他们甚至调整了它的方向，让它永远面向莫斯科。

sentences.en: So are these pictures you're showing me from when it was erected or did people come afterward to check it out?
sentences.zh: 所以你给我看的这些照片是它刚竖起时的，还是人们后来去检查时拍的？

sentences.en: Like, you know, how inaccessible is the Lenin at the pole of inaccessibility?
sentences.zh: 就像，不访问极上的列宁到底有多难接近？

sentences.en: He's pretty inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 他相当难接近。

sentences.en: Well, these photos are the originals.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些照片是原版的。

sentences.en: There was a brief spurt of visits by pole of inaccessibility standards in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 按照不访问极的标准，在 20 世纪 60 年代曾有过短暂的访问高潮。

sentences.en: The Soviets went back super briefly in 64.
sentences.zh: 苏联人在 64 年非常短暂地回过一次。

sentences.en: Then in 65, an American research team dropped by, climbed up the pedestal and swiveled the bus so that Lenin faced towards Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 然后在 65 年，一个美国研究团队顺道来访，爬上底座，把半身像转了个方向，让列宁面向华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: At which point, learning of the American antics, the Soviets came back down one last time and swiveled him back towards Moscow.
sentences.zh: 得知美国人的恶作剧后，苏联人最后一次返回，又把他转回了面向莫斯科的方向。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an aspect of the Cold War that I can totally get behind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是冷战的一个方面，我完全可以理解。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, if the whole Cold War was just like somehow like dueling pranks for the sake of like national pride, that would be a much better.
sentences.zh: 如果整个冷战只是一场为了国家荣誉而进行的恶作剧对决，那会好得多。

sentences.en: After that little back and forth, after that little duel, for many, many decades, there was nothing.
sentences.zh: 经过那几次来来回回的较量之后，在长达几十年的时间里，这里什么都没有发生。

sentences.en: The southern POI went kind of forgotten and unvisited,
sentences.zh: 南半球的不访问极有点被遗忘了，无人问津，

sentences.en: which means that all through the rest of the Cold War and perestroika and the fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of the Soviet Union,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在整个冷战剩余的时间里、在经济改革、柏林墙倒塌和苏联解体期间，

sentences.en: and as all the other statues and busts of Lenin were being toppled all over the world, this one lonely Lenin just sat there untouched by the forces of history.
sentences.zh: 当世界上所有其他的列宁雕像和半身像都被推倒时，这个孤独的列宁却静静地坐在那里，未受历史洪流的影响。

sentences.en: So it wasn't toppled, you know, by people marking the end of the regime, but did, you know, nature topple it eventually?
sentences.zh: 所以它没有被那些标志着政权结束的人推倒，但大自然最终把它推倒了吗？

sentences.en: Like, what is the fate of Lenin on the POI?
sentences.zh: 列宁在不访问极上的命运究竟如何？

sentences.en: So this is where the story takes a turn.
sentences.zh: 故事在这里迎来了转折。

sentences.en: Because when people finally returned to the area in the mid-2000s, the official position of the POI had actually changed in the intervening years due to like updated calculations.
sentences.zh: 因为当人们在 2000 年代中期终于重返该地区时，由于更新了计算方式，在过去的几年里，不访问极的官方位置实际上已经改变了。

sentences.en: So the new focus was on being the first to go to these new coordinates and nab that record.
sentences.zh: 所以新的焦点是成为第一个到达这些新坐标并夺得这一纪录的人。

sentences.en: And checking up on Lenin to see if he was still kicking, it just wasn't a priority.
sentences.zh: 而去看望列宁看看他还好不好，已经不再是当务之急了。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, there was at least one person who continued to believe that Lenin was still there at the old POI and could be found.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，仍然至少有一个人坚信列宁依然在旧的不访问极上，并且可以找到。

sentences.en: There's no way I was ever going to let go of it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不可能放弃它。

sentences.en: So one way or other, I was, you know, crawling to the pole of inaccessibility.
sentences.zh: 所以不管怎样，你知道的，我当时在向不可接近极艰难地进发。

sentences.en: I was always going there.
sentences.zh: 我本来就是要去那里的。

sentences.en: So who is that?
sentences.zh: 那他是谁？

sentences.en: So that is Henry Cookson.
sentences.zh: 那就是亨利·库克森。

sentences.en: And today he runs an adventure travel outfit called Cookson Adventures.
sentences.zh: 如今他经营着一家名为“库克森探险”的探险旅游公司。

sentences.en: But back in 2006, he was not a professional adventurer.
sentences.zh: 但在2006年的时候，他还不是一名职业探险家。

sentences.en: He was just kind of a random dude who, along with two other friends, Rupert Longsdon and Rory Sweet,
sentences.zh: 他只是个偶然的家伙，和另外两个朋友鲁珀特·隆斯顿和罗里·斯威特一起，

sentences.en: just kind of got obsessed with finding this bust of Lenin at the Southern Pole of inaccessibility.
sentences.zh: 迷上了寻找南极不可接近极的这座列宁半身像。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: None of us had a clue.
sentences.zh: 我们谁也不知道情况。

sentences.en: I had my teammates.
sentences.zh: 我有我的队友们。

sentences.en: We didn't know where the north, south.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道北方在哪里，南方在哪里。

sentences.en: We didn't know where the penguins were north or south.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道企鹅是在北边还是南边。

sentences.en: We didn't know the polar bears.
sentences.zh: 我们对北极熊一无所知。

sentences.en: We knew nothing about these areas.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些地区一无所知。

sentences.en: He sounds like the right man for the job.
sentences.zh: 他听起来正是这份工作的合适人选。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I actually do firmly believe in beginner's luck.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我实际上确实坚信新手运这回事。

sentences.en: Like, you don't know you're not supposed to do certain things.
sentences.zh: 比如，你不知道有些事情是不该做的。

sentences.en: So you just do them and then you kind of get away with them.
sentences.zh: 所以你只管去做，然后往往就能蒙混过关。

sentences.en: Everyone else they consulted with basically said, why even bother at this point?
sentences.zh: 他们咨询过的其他人基本上都说，这会儿还费这劲干嘛？

sentences.en: Because even if you get there, you're not going to find anything.
sentences.zh: 因为即使你们到了那里，也什么都找不到。

sentences.en: They just looked at us and said, look, Lenin is going to be buried under the snow.
sentences.zh: 他们看着我们说，听着，列宁肯定已经被埋在雪底下了。

sentences.en: You know, huge structures have been buried over the decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，几十年来巨大的建筑都被埋掉了。

sentences.en: So a small little statue that no one's been to in 40, 50 years, you know, without doubt, it's not going to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以这么一个小雕像，40、50年都没人去过了，毫无疑问，它肯定不在那儿了。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So they could be right on it, right there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能就站在它旁边，就在那儿。

sentences.en: But Lenin could be so buried they would not actually find it.
sentences.zh: 但列宁可能被埋得太深，以至于他们实际上根本找不到它。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they hired a fourth person, a veteran Antarctic explorer named Paul Landry, to help supervise their team.
sentences.zh: 于是他们雇用了第四个人，一位资深的南极探险家名叫保罗·兰德里，来帮助监督他们的团队。

sentences.en: But there was still this complication because even though great parts of the Antarctic ice sheet are, you know, calving away due to climate change,
sentences.zh: 但仍然存在这样一个复杂情况，因为尽管南极冰盖的很大一部分由于气候变化正在崩解，

sentences.en: the middle of the continent, the snow is still just accumulating and then compacts down into ice.
sentences.zh: 但在大陆中部，雪仍在不断堆积，然后压实成冰。

sentences.en: And at the pole of inaccessibility, one of the things that makes it a challenging place to go is that the ice there is, I believe, 13,000 feet deep.
sentences.zh: 而在不可接近极，让它成为一个充满挑战的地方的原因之一，就是那里的冰厚度，我相信达到了13000英尺。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, despite the odds, they decided to go look for Lenin.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，不顾重重困难，他们还是决定去找列宁。

sentences.en: And so they went down to Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了南极洲。

sentences.en: They used kites to help pull themselves and their supplies across the ice.
sentences.zh: 他们用风筝拉着自己和物资横跨冰原。

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I will skip over the details of the journey itself.
sentences.zh: 对，我略过这段旅程本身的细节。

sentences.en: You know, insert your standard extremes of Antarctica statistics here.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，此处请自行脑补南极洲的标准极端统计数据。

sentences.en: But I will just say that to reach the suspected location of the Russian station took them 46 days.
sentences.zh: 但我只想说，为了到达那个俄罗斯科考站的疑似地点，他们花了46天。

sentences.en: Holy moly.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天呐。

sentences.en: The whole way there was just pure horizon.
sentences.zh: 一路上全都是纯粹的地平线。

sentences.en: You know, an almost entirely flat, featureless landscape.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，几乎是一片完全平坦、毫无特征的风景。

sentences.en: And all through this monotonous journey, they had to contend with the possibility that when they got to the coordinates,
sentences.zh: 在这一路单调的旅程中，他们不得不面对这样一种可能性：当他们到达坐标时，

sentences.en: Lenin would be so buried in the snow that all they would see was more flat, featureless landscape.
sentences.zh: 列宁会深深地埋在雪中，以至于他们看到的只有更多平坦、毫无特征的风景。

sentences.en: We'd only seen white, you know, white snow and sky on our own selves and tent for the last 50-odd days.
sentences.zh: 在过去的50多天里，我们眼中只看到白色，白色的雪和天空，以及我们自己和帐篷。

sentences.en: And we reach the said coordinates.
sentences.zh: 然后我们到达了所谓的坐标点。

sentences.en: We are absolutely exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: We're freezing cold.
sentences.zh: 我们冷得要命。

sentences.en: And we can see nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么也看不见。

sentences.en: So, you know, we agreed to keep on pushing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们一致同意继续坚持。

sentences.en: And after a few minutes, I see this tiny little black dot on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，我看到地平线上有一个极小的黑点。

sentences.en: A few more minutes and this little black dot starts to grow into something more substantial.
sentences.zh: 又过了几分钟，这个小黑点开始变成更实在的东西。

sentences.en: And then suddenly you can make out, you know, the outline of a man.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间你能辨认出，你知道的，一个人的轮廓。

sentences.en: And there was this silence.
sentences.zh: 四周一片寂静。

sentences.en: We put down our kites and we just walked.
sentences.zh: 我们放下风筝，只是默默地走着。

sentences.en: We walked in silence up to this statue.
sentences.zh: 我们默默地走向这座雕像。

sentences.en: And there was Lenin.
sentences.zh: 列宁就在那里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I cannot believe they found him.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信他们找到了他。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们真的找到了。

sentences.en: He wasn't buried under the snow.
sentences.zh: 他没有被埋在雪底下。

sentences.en: At least not yet.
sentences.zh: 至少还没完全埋住。

sentences.en: And I have to say, I just I just love this part of the story because here's a photo of what Lenin looked like when when they did find him.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我就是喜欢故事的这一部分，因为这里有一张照片，展示了他们找到列宁时的样子。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's really just the top of the chimney that's left and the buSt.
sentences.zh: 所以真的只剩下烟囱的顶部和半身像了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's he's just barely hanging on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他简直是勉强支撑。

sentences.en: It's been reduced to a kind of I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他已经缩水成了一种，我不知道。

sentences.en: What do you call it?
sentences.zh: 你叫它什么？

sentences.en: Like a plinth?
sentences.zh: 像个柱座？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To give you a sense of scale.
sentences.zh: 为了让你对比例有个概念。

sentences.en: Well, the snow had been accumulating, obviously, in the previous 48 years, but it hadn't quite made it all the way up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然在过去的48年里雪一直在积聚，但还没完全漫上来。

sentences.en: The original chimney of the Russian station was maybe, let's say, 30 feet high.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯科考站原本的烟囱大概有，比方说，30英尺高。

sentences.en: And now only about six to seven feet were left, making Lenin at that pole of inaccessibility a tad more accessible.
sentences.zh: 现在只剩下大约六到七英尺，这使得南极不可接近极的这座列宁像稍微变得更容易接近了一点。

sentences.en: You can reach up and touch it.
sentences.zh: 你伸手就能摸到它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which is exactly what they did.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们所做的。

sentences.en: The really bizarre thing was, you know, we was expecting this to be a bronze or something, you know, a sture.
sentences.zh: 真正离谱的是，你知道的，我们原本以为这是青铜什么的，你知道的，是一尊雕像。

sentences.en: And it was made of some sort of weird yellow plastic compound, which is very light.
sentences.zh: 结果它是由某种奇怪的黄色塑料复合材料制成的，非常轻。

sentences.en: You could you could pick him up.
sentences.zh: 你可以，你可以把他抱起来。

sentences.en: Did you pick him up?
sentences.zh: 你们把他抱起来了吗？

sentences.en: You could.
sentences.zh: 你可以的。

sentences.en: We did pick him up.
sentences.zh: 我们确实把他抱起来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Did they make him face towards London or something?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有让他面向伦敦什么的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, of course, I asked Henry precisely that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我当然向亨利确切地问了这一点。

sentences.en: And he said, no, they left him facing towards Moscow, but not before goofing around just a bit.
sentences.zh: 他说，没有，他们让他面向莫斯科，但在那之前稍微胡闹了一会儿。

sentences.en: He might have been dressed up a little bit, you know, nothing, nothing too irreverent.
sentences.zh: 他可能稍微被装扮了一下，你知道的，没什么，没有什么太不敬的。

sentences.en: You know, we, we, we put it, we put a sort of hat on him and some goggles and, and, and some took some pictures of us all sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们，我们，我们在他头上戴了某种帽子，还有一些护目镜，然后，拍了一些我们大家聚在一起，你知道的，

sentences.en: group huddle around him and everything else.
sentences.zh: 围在他周围拥作一团之类的照片。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think he's, he's, he's left with his, his pride intact.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我觉得他，他，他保留了他的尊严。

sentences.en: I'm glad they left his pride intact, but it sounds like he's not going to last for that much longer because if the ice has accumulated around, you know,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴他们保留了他的尊严，但听起来他撑不了多久了，因为如果冰在50年里积聚了大约，你知道的，

sentences.en: 20 feet in the 50 years and there's only about six feet left, it seems like Lenin will be gone in another decade or so.
sentences.zh: 20英尺，而现在只剩下大约六英尺，看起来列宁在再一个十年左右就会消失。

sentences.en: Could you remind me when his expedition was?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我他的探险是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Henry's expedition was, um, December of 2006 is when they started.
sentences.zh: 亨利的探险是，嗯，他们是2006年12月出发的。

sentences.en: They found Lenin, um, in January of 2007.
sentences.zh: 他们找到列宁是在，嗯，2007年1月。

sentences.en: So it's already like, you know, 13, 14 years.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经，你知道的，有13、14年了。

sentences.en: And so do people know if Lenin is still there?
sentences.zh: 那么人们知道列宁是否还在那里吗？

sentences.en: Is it almost up for Lenin?
sentences.zh: 列宁快要撑不住了吗？

sentences.en: So of course that's the big question, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这当然是最大的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And as it turns out, the Russian station has been visited at least two more times since then.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，自那以后，俄罗斯科考站至少又被参观过两次。

sentences.en: And of course, each set of visitors took the obligatory photo posing next to Lenin.
sentences.zh: 当然，每一批游客都拍了在列宁旁边摆姿势的必修照片。

sentences.en: So here's a photo of a Norwegian team that got there just one year later in 2008.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一张挪威团队的照片，他们在一年后的2008年到达了那里。

sentences.en: Oh, so yeah, he's already lost a foot, at least, you know, maybe, maybe two or three feet.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以是的，他已经失去了一只脚，至少，你知道的，也许，也许两三英尺。

sentences.en: The bottom of the, or the top of the plinth, right where the bus starts is just about chest height on most of these guys.
sentences.zh: 基座的底部，或者说顶部，也就是半身像开始的地方，对大多数这些家伙来说大约齐胸高。

sentences.en: I'd say it shaved off.
sentences.zh: 我可以说它被削掉了一截。

sentences.en: Let's go with a foot.
sentences.zh: 就算是一英尺吧。

sentences.en: I think a foot, foot and a head.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是一英尺，一英尺加一个头。

sentences.en: But, um, even more recent data, much more recent data is from this photo taken by a solo Australian adventurer who went, basically he went yesterday.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，更新的数据，更新得多的数据来自这张照片，是一个澳大利亚单人探险家拍的，他基本上是昨天去的。

sentences.en: This photo was taken in December of 2019.
sentences.zh: 这张照片拍摄于2019年12月。

sentences.en: And this one looks like a, like maybe two foot off the ground.
sentences.zh: 这张看起来离地面大概，大概只有两英尺了。

sentences.en: He's sitting in this photo, but if he stood up, he would be taller.
sentences.zh: 他在照片里是坐着的，但如果他站起来，他会更高。

sentences.en: Above it.
sentences.zh: 比它高。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Much taller.
sentences.zh: 高得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I do, I do think that this like kind of drab cookie cutter Lenin with its standard issue, defiant expression is the perfect statue for this situation.
sentences.zh: 我确实，我确实觉得这种单调乏味的千篇一律的列宁雕像，带着标准的不服输的表情，是这种境况下的完美雕像。

sentences.en: Like, you know, cause like he never looks worried.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，因为他看起来从不担心。

sentences.en: Like even as the ice encroaches, he, he seems to just be saying like, you know, bring it on.
sentences.zh: 就像即使冰层侵袭，他，他似乎也只是在说，放马过来吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's definitely, he's facing his fate with a sort of admirable stoicism, but like, but his fate is coming no matter what.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是带着一种令人钦佩的坚忍在面对自己的命运，但是，但是他的命运无论如何都会降临。

sentences.en: I mean, like if I were to guess, like it, it did about another, uh, foot in a, or two feet in a year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我来猜的话，它，一年大概又矮了，呃，一英尺或者两英尺。

sentences.en: I mean, you're talking five years max before he's like gone for good.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最多五年他就要彻底消失了。

sentences.en: Is there any notion that, you know, you should save him?
sentences.zh: 有没有人觉得，你知道，你们应该救救他？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just a plasticine bust of Lenin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一尊列宁的塑料半身像。

sentences.en: I mean, could they just like take him or what do you think will happen?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们难道不能直接把他带走吗？或者你觉得会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, it would be a treaty violation, um, yeah, Antarctica is under the joint jurisdiction, um, of the signatories of the Antarctic treaty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，这会违反条约，嗯，是的，南极洲受南极条约签字国的共同管辖。

sentences.en: And in 2012, the signatories approved a list of historic sites and monuments to be preserved.
sentences.zh: 2012年，签字国批准了一份需要保护的历史遗迹和纪念碑名单。

sentences.en: And there's a lot actually there for like 86 monuments on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 其实上面有很多，名单上有86处纪念碑。

sentences.en: 86 monuments on Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 南极洲有86处纪念碑。

sentences.en: Let me just tell you, there's a surprising number of plaques in Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 我直说吧，南极洲的纪念铭牌数量惊人。

sentences.en: Plaques, which no one reads.
sentences.zh: 根本没人读的铭牌。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: But, um, you know, I think this time 99 PI can, um, forgive our listeners if they haven't, if they haven't read the, the Antarctica plaques.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，你知道的，我想这次99 PI可以，嗯，原谅我们的听众如果他们没有，如果他们没有读过南极的铭牌。

sentences.en: But coming in at number four was the bust of Lenin at the Southern Pole of Inaccessibility.
sentences.zh: 但排在第四位的是南极不可接近极的列宁半身像。

sentences.en: Oh, so this is one of the historic monuments that, that has to be preserved.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这是需要保护的历史纪念碑之一。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, if it's number four on the list, um, it's funny, you can like see them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果它在名单上排第四，嗯，这很有趣，你可以看到它们。

sentences.en: It's like, this one's like, this one is listed by Denmark and this one is listed by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 就像，这个是，这个是由丹麦列出的，这个是由美国列出的。

sentences.en: And like, this is the, I think this is either the first or second, like one listed by Russia.

sentences.en: So, OK, so, you know, so these are music games, but not like rhythm games, which I think is what a lot of people think of.

sentences.zh: 罗曼，你玩过那些游戏吗？

sentences.zh: 摇滚乐队肯定是玩过的。

sentences.zh: 就像我家有一套摇滚乐队的设备。

sentences.en: He was also an ad man in the in the 60s, and he recorded lots of kids games like he was a New Yorker and he basically was agoraphobic and he basically stuck to his block.
sentences.zh: 他在60年代也是个广告人，录制了许多儿童游戏，比如他是个纽约人，基本上有点广场恐惧症，所以他的活动范围基本局限在自己所在的街区。

sentences.en: Um, but he recorded all these clapping and kids games that were amazing.

sentences.en: And there's a kids and sisters piece about about Tony Schwartz, which is stunning and one of my favorite pieces of radio.
sentences.zh: 有一个关于托尼·施瓦茨的儿童与姐妹（Kids and Sisters）节目片段，非常震撼，是我最喜欢的广播节目之一。

sentences.en: And, uh, and so I have some different record albums of Tony Schwartz recording, uh, clapping kids games and rhyming games and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，所以我有一些托尼·施瓦茨录制的不同唱片专辑，里面有儿童拍手游戏、押韵游戏之类的内容。

sentences.en: And I think that stuff is really amazing, but I've never done that myself, you know?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些东西真的很神奇，但我自己从来没玩过，你知道吗？

sentences.zh: 我小时候也从来不是那种玩拍手游戏的小孩，但我也觉得这也是因为我只是

sentences.en: Yes, but like, I just don't, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，但是，我就是不，你知道，

sentences.en: and I think this is why music composing games really appeal to me is because so what's different about a music composing game is that there are like rules around it, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么音乐创作游戏真的很吸引我，因为音乐创作游戏的不同之处在于它周围有一些规则，你知道，

sentences.en: keep it sounding like music or, you know, or like whatever the game determines is music.
sentences.zh: 让它听起来像音乐，或者，你知道，或者像游戏所定义的音乐那样。

sentences.en: But the whole idea behind them is that you get something different every single time you play, you know,
sentences.zh: 但它们背后的整个理念是，你每次玩都会得到完全不同的结果，你知道，

sentences.en: and there are lots of different examples of how people construct ways of like basically generating songs and generating like different kinds of like song experiences from a set of rules.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多不同的例子，展示了人们如何构建各种方法，基本上是从一套规则中生成歌曲和不同种类的歌曲体验。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: And some of these examples are a little less, maybe historically significant than others, but this is my personal museum we're about to step into.
sentences.zh: 其中一些例子可能在历史上没有那么重要，但这是我们即将走进的我的个人博物馆。

sentences.en: This is my, these are my favorites.
sentences.zh: 这是我的，这些是我的最爱。

sentences.en: A composer might like lay out like a certain number of notes or maybe write like a few different like melody variations.
sentences.zh: 作曲家可能会列出一定数量的音符，或者写几个不同的旋律变体。

sentences.en: And then they kind of like write them on sheets of paper, maybe, or like assign, you know, and assign numbers to them.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可能会把它们写在纸上，或者分配，你知道的，给它们分配编号。

sentences.en: And then you roll some dice and then you like notate based on what numbers you roll.
sentences.zh: 然后你掷骰子，根据你掷出的数字来进行记谱。

sentences.en: And so basically you're making a song through chance.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上你是通过机缘巧合来创作一首歌。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, like you may, you may have even like written sections of music, but how one goes into the other and how the song starts and is like,

sentences.zh: 完全基于掷骰子的运气。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's the kind of thing that you could use maybe as like a writing prompt to like to, you know, to be like, oh, I'm, I'm totally stuck right now.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一种你可以用来作为写作灵感的东西，比如，你知道，会觉得，“哦，我现在完全卡壳了。”

sentences.en: Well, I'll just like, well, I like these notes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只会，嗯，我喜欢这些音符。

sentences.en: I guess maybe I'll just like see if I can like, just like leave it up to God.
sentences.zh: 我想也许我只是看看能不能，就像顺其自然交给上帝吧。

sentences.en: And I really like that because it sounds like a good way to maybe just like get yourself out of your own way when you're like, you know, when you're working on something.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这样，因为这听起来是一个好方法，当你（在创作时）卡住的时候，能帮你跳出自己的思维定势。

sentences.en: And I, you know, as someone who has like deadlines for music, like I, I've never tried doing that, but I'm like, I'm very interested in like seeing how that could play out.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，作为一个有音乐截稿日期的人，我，我从来没试过那样做，但我真的很想看看这会如何发展。
